### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b416147940989130809f4adc6c66c52b032f00e0` — the merge of head `1234236ab8fe2060cd98c1558a3570839786eee4` into base `75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b416147940989130809f4adc6c66c52b032f00e0 && git checkout b416147940989130809f4adc6c66c52b032f00e0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8 1234236ab8fe2060cd98c1558a3570839786eee4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8 && git merge --no-ff 1234236ab8fe2060cd98c1558a3570839786eee4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1234236ab8fe2060cd98c1558a3570839786eee4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/identity-assignment-body-writes.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.hook-action-body-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/identity-assignment-body-writes.test.ts, .changeset/25653-hook-action-body-identity-assignment-write-refused.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (ObjectRepository), packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-automation-identity-write-refusal.integration.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook-body.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The run-time gate today, and what this PR adds.** `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts` refuses a governed write (`GOVERNED_OPERATIONS`: insert, update, delete, transfer, restore, purge) to the four objects when the context carries `isSystem` AND (`flowRunId` OR the `@objectstack/core` app-automation elevation mark). The middleware calls it ahead of its `isSystem` bypass (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, the block before line 320). After #25954 and #25982 the mark covers a `runAs: 'system'` hook, an app-authored hook's inherited system context and its `sudo()`, an action body, and `ObjectRepository.execute()`. So the card's two run-time paths are closed on `main`, and the card's remaining ask (its "Save-time" line, retriage 6431012701: the save-time refusal, the `Hook.runAs` sentence, the D3 entry) is exactly this diff. `Fixes #25653` is right. Correct.
2. **Evasion of the save-time check.** The reader is a literal match: `.object(` with a single-quoted, double-quoted or backtick literal of one of the four names, followed by one of six write verbs, on the handle or on a `const`/`let`/`var` the body bound it to. A dynamic name (`ctx.api.object(name)`), concatenation (`'sys_' + 'member'`), a destructured `object`, bracket access, a reassignment without a declaration, or a handle returned by a function all pass the parse. None of them passes at run time: the write arrives at the middleware as an operation on the real object name under a marked context and is refused there. This is the shape the card ruled ("a hook or action whose body literally names one of the four objects"), the #21687 precedent, and the D3 entry says "named with one of the four as a literal". The run-time refusal stays the enforcement; the parse is the authoring door. Correct, with the limit stated in the entry.
3. **Verb set.** The six verbs (`insert`, `update`, `delete`, `updateMany`, `deleteMany`, `upsert`) are byte-for-byte the `WRITE` list the sandbox installs on `ctx.api.object(name)` (`quickjs-runner.ts` line 686); the sandbox hands them to `ObjectRepository`, which carries `insert`, `update`, `delete` and no `upsert`/`updateMany`/`deleteMany` (those three fault "not implemented" in the sandbox), so judging them is conservative and harmless. The reads (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`) are not judged, as at run time. `ctx.api.sudo()` does not exist in the sandbox, so it needs no reading. A write inside `ctx.api.transaction(fn)` whose callback does `api.object('sys_member').insert(…)` is caught: the handle pattern takes any prefix before `.object(`. Correct.
4. **What is now refused, and who carries it.** Only a hook with `runAs: 'system'` and a `language: 'js'` body, or a `type: 'script'` action with such a body. A hook under `'user'` or `'inherit'`, an expression body (no IO), a code `handler`, and every other object stay accepted; pinned by the controls. An `'inherit'` hook that a platform system write elevates cannot be judged by a parse and is left to the run-time mark, which is right. Census on the tree: `.object(` with any of the four names in any quote form hits only `packages/objectql/src/hook-run-as.test.ts` (in-process handler code, not a body string) and two prose pages under `content/docs/permissions/`; nothing in `examples/`, showcase apps, templates or fixtures. The run-time pins in `packages/runtime/src/app-automation-identity-write-refusal.integration.test.ts` build exactly the refused shape, but through `bindHooksToEngine`, which does not parse with `HookSchema` (`hook-binder.ts` line 379), so they survive. hotcrm was not measured in this session or by the dev; the server slices' census found none there.
5. **Doors.** `HookSchema`, the registered `hook` type schema (the metadata save door), `ActionSchema`, the registered `action` type schema, `defineStack` (422 `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` at `hooks.N.body.source`) and the artifact stage (`safeExtend` keeps the superRefine) are each pinned. `ActionSchema` is a `.refine(...)` chain, so the new `.superRefine` runs beside the existing ones; its position before the feature-gate term keeps the convention the comment names. Correct.
6. **Refusal text names a remedy.** One `custom` issue per object at `body.source`; for the two assignment tables it says set `runAs: 'user'` (hook) or move the grant to a `runAs: 'user'` flow (action); for invitations and memberships it names the four organization endpoints. Same routing as the run-time refusal. Correct.
7. **False positives.** A comment or string that spells `ctx.api.object('sys_member').insert(` refuses the body, and a shadowed binding name can refuse a body that writes another object. Both are conservative and both carry the remedy; the test's "reads stay legal" control shows the common case is not caught by accident. Not blocking.
8. **Docs truth.** `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx` is regenerated from the new `.describe()` and is true at the head: the governed-write list matches `GOVERNED_OPERATIONS`, the code is `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the save-time sentence matches the refinement. The `FlowSchema.runAs` sentence it mirrors is at `flow.zod.ts` line 1183. The action reference did not change because the `body` `.describe()` did not change (only its JSDoc); that is consistent.
9. **Public face.** The leaf is not exported from the barrel; the test imports it by path. The accept set of two published schemas narrows; no key is added, removed or re-shaped; no error code is minted. The four-object set and the prescription text now exist in the spec leaf and in plugin-security's `FLOW_SYSTEM_IDENTITY_WRITE_OBJECTS`; the dev names it in the PR's acceptance notes. Not blocking.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `@objectstack/spec: minor`, title `feat(spec)!:`, a `**BREAKING**` banner with Before/Now/Fix, `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — …` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed (…)`. The PR body carries the same two lines. `clause2-line.mjs` reads the arm as the first token inside the parenthetical and keeps trailing reasoning (lines 269 to 273), and `readMetadataProtocolLine` reads `narrowed` and ignores the parenthetical (lines 553 to 556). `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: a declared `narrowing` is BREAKING and ships `minor` in the launch window (lines 1793 to 1840); `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm is the consistent pair. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The level and the declarations agree.
- The claim 6431680234 reads `Clause-②: no` with no arm, while the PR and changeset read `no (narrowing)`. The dev declared the deviation in the report. The review judges the PR body and the changeset, which agree; the claim line is the seat's own and should be amended to `no (narrowing)` so the three carriers match (③ item 2).
- ADR-0087: entry id `hook-action-body-system-identity-assignment-write-refused`, file `18.hook-action-body-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts`, the same `18.id.ts` rule as its neighbour `18.flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused.ts`; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `18.0.0`, so step 18 is the open step. `registry.ts` is generated by `build-migration-registry.ts` from a `readdir` of `entries/semantic`, so no registry edit is owed, and the test reads the entry from `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18]`. The changeset marker `adr-0087: registered hook-action-body-system-identity-assignment-write-refused` names only the id this diff adds, which is the check's rule. No `conversionIds` and a "NOT convertible" reason, the same disposition as the neighbour; no tombstone, pinned. `surface` carries no backticks and no pipes. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question (APP_AUTOMATION_ELEVATION as a declared `ExecutionContext` field).** The dev recommends A (keep the core symbol). Answer: agreed for this PR. A parse judges metadata, not a context, so nothing here reads the mark, and a declared field would be a protocol addition that triage 6431012701 says returns to triage first. Nothing owed on this head.
2. **Claim line.** The claim's `Clause-②: no` lacks the `(narrowing)` arm the PR and changeset carry. The seat amends the claim; no change to the diff.
3. **Prose that still reads unqualified.** `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx` line 157 calls `runAs: 'system'` "a full-access, RLS-bypassing system principal"; `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` line 443 says an action body "bypass[es] row- and field-level security by design"; `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` line 185 says a hook elevates itself with `runAs`. None names the four-object exception. The run-time slices left `flows.mdx` the same way and put the fact on `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 1b, and the reference page now carries it for hooks. One sentence in `hooks.mdx` and `ui/actions.mdx` (and the automation skill) is owed as a docs follow-up; the prose face is the lane seat's ACCEPT, not this review's gate.
4. **Dev-flagged, out of this card.** `FlowSchema` has no save-time twin (a system flow's write node aimed at the four objects is refused only at run time); the set and prescription text live twice (spec leaf, plugin-security). Both named in the PR's acceptance notes; neither is in the card's ask. Follow-ups.
5. **Dogfood reds on `main`.** The dev's full battery shows 10 failures in `test/authz-conformance.test.ts` and `test/authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` from #26361, an ancestor of the base; this diff touches nothing under `packages/rest` or `packages/qa`. Not this PR's.
6. **Author.** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.
7. **CI on the head at review time.** Green: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, CI release and engine gates, three scoped), Spec property liveness, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Plan Test Core shards, filter. Skipped (opt-in or matrix): 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood matrix shards. Still in progress at the last read (47 runs, 0 non-green, 13 pending): Test Core 1 to 8, Build Core, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI. Nothing on the head is red. The landing pre-check (every check green) is the seat's, once those finish; this verdict judges the contract, and the seat re-reads the head's check-runs before the queue.
